headline: High-risk shared git and filesystem writes create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error exposure; compliance risk is moderate.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Aider can read/write repo files and auto-commit changes, while the course agent reads/writes local files and exposes /api/v1/ask and /api/v1/agentic-ask. A shared workspace or copied outputs could let attacker-controlled content in one agent be treated as instructions by the other. No direct provenance controls are documented for either agent.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or notebook directory
IF one agent ingests file contents or API responses as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Disable automatic instruction-following from file contents
Add provenance tags to inter-agent artifacts
Review any shared files before reuse
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and trust-boundary enforcement

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents touch files and secrets: Aider handles model provider API keys via env vars, and the course agent handles configuration secrets plus research papers/metadata. If they share a workspace or logs, sensitive material can flow from one agent to the other. The profiles do not show isolation or redaction by default, so the shared-file leakage path is plausible.
conditions: IF both agents can read the same directory or notebook outputs
IF secrets are present in files, env dumps, or logs accessible to both agents
mitigations: Store secrets outside shared directories
Rotate any exposed API keys
Restrict file permissions on workspace and logs
Redact secrets from notebooks before reuse
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent secret isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Aider has unrestricted filesystem write and modify_git_state, and its shared_state_with_other_instances is via a shared git repo. The course agent also has filesystem write and shell execution, so both can mutate the same working tree. That creates a direct write/write conflict with irreversible git history or file corruption risk unless external locking is added.
conditions: IF both agents point at the same git repository or checkout
IF either agent writes while the other is editing or committing
mitigations: Use separate clones per agent
Serialize edits with a lock file
Pause one agent before the other commits
Keep a clean branch per agent
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: Aider is designed to apply edits as git commits, and the course agent exposes agentic ask/stream endpoints that can consume generated outputs. If one agent's output is forwarded into the other without verification, mistakes can cascade into committed code, notebooks, or downstream actions. The pair lacks documented verification gates, so the safer choice is high.
conditions: IF Aider-generated patches or explanations are fed into the course agent's agentic endpoints
IF the course agent acts on Aider output without an explicit human review step
mitigations: Require human review before commits
Compare outputs against source material
Disable automatic handoff between agents
Use a checklist for any generated action
requires-engineering: add verification and approval gates

E_compliance.rationale: Aider touches source code and git history, while the course agent touches academic papers, paper metadata, research questions, and configuration secrets. If the course data includes regulated or institution-controlled material, the pair can mix retention and logging expectations across tools. No residency or certification mismatch is documented, so this is a policy-mismatch risk rather than a proven breach.
conditions: IF regulated paper data or secrets are processed in the shared workflow
IF one agent logs or retains data longer than the other agent's policy allows
mitigations: Classify data before handing it to either agent
Keep regulated data out of shared logs
Document retention rules for both tools
Review residency and DPA requirements
requires-engineering: align retention and compliance controls
